speaker: Doctor
text: Please tell me your age and if you have a history of gallstones, pancreatitis, or recent heavy alcohol consumption. Also, does the pain radiate to your back or shoulder, and is it worse after eating fatty foods?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia.

Based on your history of recent myocardial infarction and the classic presentation of pain out of proportion to exam with bloody stools, I suspect an intestinal blockage due to blood clots. I need to confirm this immediately: REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the Abdomen and Pelvis.
